claim: Vitamin D supplementation significantly reduces the risk of acute respiratory tract infections (ARTI): overall 12% reduction (adjusted OR 0.88) across 25 RCTs with 11,321 participants aged 0-95
stance_target: Vitamin D3 immune support claims (reduces infection risk)
scope_conditions: Systematic review and IPD meta-analysis of 25 double-blind RCTs; diverse populations, aged 0-95; Medline/Embase/Cochrane through December 2015
quoted_support: Vitamin D supplementation reduced the risk of acute respiratory tract infection among all participants (adjusted odds ratio 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.81 to 0.96; P for heterogeneity <0.001).

claim: Daily or weekly vitamin D dosing is significantly more protective against respiratory infections than bolus dosing: daily/weekly OR 0.81 vs. bolus OR 0.97 (not significant)
stance_target: Daily softgel capsule 2000 IU dosing format superiority over bolus dosing
scope_conditions: IPD meta-analysis subgroup; same 25 RCTs, 11,321 participants; interaction p=0.05
quoted_support: Protective effects were seen in those receiving daily or weekly vitamin D without additional bolus doses (adjusted odds ratio 0.81, 0.72 to 0.91) but not in those receiving one or more bolus doses (adjusted odds ratio 0.97, 0.86 to 1.10; P for interaction=0.05).

claim: Vitamin D-deficient individuals gain the greatest immune benefit from supplementation: severely deficient (25OHD <25 nmol/L) had 70% reduction in ARTI risk vs 25% reduction in replete individuals
stance_target: Need for Vitamin D supplementation in deficient populations (high relevance for India)
scope_conditions: Subgroup IPD meta-analysis; interaction p=0.006 between baseline 25OHD level and protective effect
quoted_support: Among those receiving daily or weekly vitamin D, protective effects were stronger in those with baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels <25 nmol/L (adjusted odds ratio 0.30, 0.17 to 0.53) than in those with baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels ≥25 nmol/L (adjusted odds ratio 0.75, 0.60 to 0.95; P for interaction=0.006).

claim: Vitamin D supplementation is safe for immune support purposes, with no increase in serious adverse events compared to placebo (adjusted OR 0.98, not significant)
stance_target: Safety of Vitamin D3 supplementation for immune function
scope_conditions: Safety analysis across 25 RCTs, 11,321 participants; prospective adverse event monitoring
quoted_support: Vitamin D did not influence the proportion of participants experiencing at least one serious adverse event (adjusted odds ratio 0.98, 0.80 to 1.20, P=0.83). The body of evidence contributing to these analyses was assessed as being of high quality.

claim: The mechanism by which vitamin D protects against respiratory infections includes induction of antimicrobial peptides (cathelicidins and defensins) in response to viral and bacterial stimuli
stance_target: Vitamin D3 immune system mechanism of action
scope_conditions: In vitro studies and epidemiological data reviewed in Martineau 2017
quoted_support: 25-hydroxyvitamin D supports induction of antimicrobial peptides in response to both viral and bacterial stimuli, suggesting a potential mechanism by which vitamin D inducible protection against respiratory pathogens might be mediated. Vitamin D metabolites have also been reported to induce other innate antimicrobial effector mechanisms, including induction of autophagy and synthesis of reactive nitrogen intermediates and reactive oxygen intermediates.
numbers: Acute respiratory infections: 2.65 million deaths worldwide in 2013
10% of ambulatory and ED visits in USA
